about: Functional coverage benchmark (ADR-0063, audit v2 N-01/F-01/F-14). Band A: a request the catalogue covers (one recipe, only functions it advertises). Band B: a covered recipe plus 1-2 capabilities the library does not have (the scope gate removes them; the covered part is built after approval). `expect` lists the canonical criteria a reviewer expects the request to map to (labelled before any run); `removed` the parts band B must drop. Written for this benchmark only (2026-10-16); not used in any test.

statements.prompt: Online booking for Hilo Tattoo studio in Seville with three artists. Clients choose a session (consultation 30 min, small piece 60 min, large piece 180 min), an artist or any artist, and a free time without an account. They get a confirmation email with a cancel link; cancelling is allowed up to 48 hours before. Artists see their calendar by day and week, block days off, and can move or cancel sessions; the client is emailed each time. No two sessions for the same artist at the same time.

Appointment booking for a two-chair barber shop in Lisbon: customers pick a haircut (30 min) or haircut and beard (45 min), a barber or any barber, and a free time; no sign-up. Confirmation email with a link to cancel up to 6 hours before. Barbers see a day and week calendar and can take time off. Never double book a barber.

An online shop for a small ceramics workshop: product catalogue with photos, mugs in three colours each with its own SKU, price and stock, a cart, discount codes with an expiry date, card payments with Stripe Checkout, order confirmation emails, stock reduced on each sale, and an admin panel to manage products and see orders.

Task management for a 6-person design agency: projects with tasks, each task has an assignee, a priority and a due date; a kanban board per project (to do, in progress, done); comments on tasks; overdue tasks are flagged; everyone has a 'my tasks' list.
A personal water and sleep tracker: set a daily goal per tracker, log amounts quickly from the dashboard, see the current streak of days meeting the goal, a 30-day history and the weekly total.

A landing page for 'Quill', an upcoming note-taking app: hero, benefits, how it works and FAQ, a waitlist form with name and email, a confirmation email to people who join, and an admin page listing the signups.
Website for an architecture firm: home, services, about us, a blog with RSS, a contact form, and an admin panel where staff edit the site texts, publish posts and read contact messages.

A client portal for an accounting firm: clients submit requests (tax return, invoice question) with PDF uploads and follow the status of each request; staff review the requests and update their status.

A sales dashboard for a team: import monthly sales from a CSV file or enter them by hand, KPIs compared with the previous period, a time series chart and a breakdown by region, filters and CSV export of the filtered data.

A small CRM SaaS: teams sign up and get their own workspace, invite nothing for now; they manage contacts (name, email, company) — create, list, edit and delete them, search contacts by name and export them to CSV. Members cannot export.

Booking site for a yoga studio: students book 60-minute classes with a teacher of their choice in a free slot, get a confirmation email with a cancel link (cancel up to 12 hours before), teachers see their week calendar and block holidays. Also: an SMS reminder 2 hours before each class.

Online appointments for a physiotherapy clinic: patients book 45-minute sessions with a physiotherapist or any, no account, confirmation email with cancellation link, no double bookings, staff day and week calendar. Plus: sync every appointment to the physiotherapist's Google Calendar.

An online store for a coffee roaster: catalogue with photos, bags in 250 g and 1 kg variants with their own price and stock, cart, Stripe Checkout, order emails, stock decremented on payment, admin panel. Also sync orders to QuickBooks.

A shop selling printed posters: product catalogue with images, cart, discount codes, payments with Stripe Checkout, shipping rates by country, order confirmation email. Plus: publish every new product automatically to our Instagram account.

Project management for a software team: projects, tasks with assignee, priority and due date, kanban board, comments, my tasks list. In addition, post a message to our Slack channel whenever a task is moved to done.
A habit tracker: daily goals, quick check-ins, streaks, a 30-day history and weekly totals. Also read my steps automatically from my Apple Watch.
A pre-launch landing page for a meal-kit startup with a waitlist form (name and email), a confirmation email and an admin list of signups. Also add every signup to our Mailchimp audience.

A portal for a law firm's clients: they submit document requests with file uploads and follow their status; lawyers review and update the status. Also notify the client on WhatsApp when the status changes.
Website for a dental clinic: home, services, about, blog with RSS, contact form, admin panel to edit content and read messages. Plus a live chat widget connected to our Zendesk account.

A marketing KPI dashboard: import campaign results from CSV, KPIs with the previous period, time series and breakdown charts, filters and CSV export. Also pull the numbers every night directly from our HubSpot account.
